summary_en: This study tests a community-based strategy called PRECEDE-PROCEED, which offers self-sampling for HPV testing to help women get cervical cancer screening. The intervention is behavioral, and how it is given, how long it lasts, and how often are not stated. The study looks at the feasibility of this approach and at factors that may influence women's decisions to join self-sample HPV testing and follow-up.
summary_es: Este estudio prueba una estrategia comunitaria llamada PRECEDE-PROCEED, que ofrece la autotoma para la prueba de VPH y así ayudar a las mujeres a hacerse el tamizaje de cáncer cervical. La intervención es conductual, y no se indica cómo se administra, cuánto dura ni con qué frecuencia. El estudio evalúa la viabilidad de este enfoque y los factores que podrían influir en la decisión de las mujeres de participar en la autotoma para la prueba de VPH y en su seguimiento.
who_for: Women age 25 or older who live in the RGV or another low-resource Texas community.
Willing to follow all study procedures and sign the consent form.
Have not had a hysterectomy that removed the cervix.
No history of cervical cancer or high-grade dysplasia.
No Pap test in the past 3.5 years, or no Pap/HPV co-test in the past 5.5 years.
not_for: Cannot communicate in English or Spanish.
